s002: I’m building an Android astronomy app with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose, bringing celestial positions, observing windows and upcoming events into one view. Right now I’m organizing data sources and the interface, and tuning gesture animations and mobile performance.
s005: My UV-K5 runs Egzumer firmware. I use it to listen to nearby repeaters and explore the spectrum, keeping notes on frequencies, antenna placement and reception. Next I want to strengthen my understanding of SDR, DSP and basic demodulation before gradually exploring HF.
s007: I’d like to bring wireless communication, IoT and deep learning together in a small project. First I’m working through signal capture, transmission and labeling; then I’ll see whether recognition and classification can actually help with everyday listening.
s010: Architecture and BIM are my day job: developing concepts, refining spaces, modeling, producing drawings and coordinating disciplines and project documents. Outside work I’m exploring contemporary Chinese architecture, especially how the empty spaces and contrasts of ink painting can become physical spaces.
s013: I’m studying audio processing, codecs and WebRTC, focusing on sample rates, latency, transmission and mobile playback. Room correction for my desktop speakers, the DAC and the rest of the signal chain are also ongoing projects.
s016: I’m gradually learning to calibrate, stack and process deep-sky images. For now I’m building a foundation in dark frames, flat fields, exposure and sensor noise.
s019: I mostly play Civilization VI, Stellaris, Hearts of Iron IV, Victoria 3, Europa Universalis IV and Crusader Kings III. Among action games, I enjoy Elden Ring, Hollow Knight, Black Myth: Wukong and The Witcher 3. I also play CS2, Arknights and Plants vs. Zombies mods. Away from the computer, I play xiangqi, shogi and chess.
s021: Key’s AIR, Kanon and CLANNAD are my three favorite visual novels; their music and stories have stayed with me for years. I’ve also loved Touhou Project for a long time: playing the original games, reading manga, collecting fan-made music and exploring its creative history. Kaguya and Plenilune Annals on this website come from that interest.
s023: I’m studying calculus, algebra, geometry, number theory, discrete mathematics and group theory at my own pace. My regular references include Thomas’ Calculus, Stein and Shakarchi’s Princeton Lectures in Analysis, and Springer’s Graduate Texts in Mathematics. I also work on ACM-style algorithm problems and AMC questions.
s025: I practice chords and fingerstyle on an acoustic guitar, and enjoy listening to music quietly. I also sketch architecture and paint with ink; the balance of emptiness and substance in ink painting influences my architectural decisions.

s038: I mainly use TArch for architectural drawings, and Revit, ArchiCAD, Civil 3D, Navisworks and BIM 360/ACC for modeling, documentation, clash detection and collaboration. For concepts and visualization, I also use SketchUp, 3ds Max, D5 Render and Lumion.
s041: I usually build Android projects in Android Studio, primarily with Kotlin and Java, using Jetpack Compose for the interface. Other projects use C, C++, Python, JavaScript, CSS and LaTeX, with Visual Studio, VS Code or JetBrains IDEs as needed. Git, Gradle, Docker and WSL support version control, builds and development environments.
s044: I work on images and vectors in Photoshop, Lightroom Classic and Illustrator, long-form layouts in InDesign, and video and audio in Premiere Pro and Audition. I use Figma for interface designs, and only occasionally open Dreamweaver to maintain older websites.
s047: My personal projects involve machine learning, computer vision and embedded systems, usually around radio signals, astronomical images or mobile devices. I care most about how data is collected and where errors come from, and only use a model when there is a clear need.

s065: ), and is the name I use in more formal settings. I chose it because Plenilune Annals is the earliest documented Chinese Touhou fan work released in Japan. That history means a great deal to me.
s067: , and is a more familiar name. I’ve loved this song for years. It feels light, clear and vivid, and I hope to carry that spirit with me, moving forward with courage and independence.
s070: I’m interested in radio communication and signal processing. I study spectrum observation, software-defined radio and basic demodulation, and explore the sounds of different bands through WebSDR.
s071: My day job is architecture and BIM, mostly concept design, modeling, drawings and coordination across disciplines. I also write Android apps, mainly with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.
s072: Outside work I listen to radio, watch the stars, study mathematics and play strategy games. I love Key and Touhou Project, play a little acoustic guitar, sketch architecture and paint with ink. Sometimes I rebuild my own architectural designs in Minecraft.
s074: Anything that mankind can gain from these stacks of paper pales in comparison to the reality offered by planting your feet on the ground or gazing up at the stars.
s075: I look forward to witnessing more miracles in the midst of the unknown, both at Rhine Lab and at Rhodes Island.

s091: When teaching myself computer science, I haven’t followed a single university’s curriculum from beginning to end. I usually use open courses to map out the topics and their order, then return to textbooks, assignments and small projects to fill the gaps.
s092: In mathematics I’m working on calculus, algebra, geometry, number theory, discrete mathematics and group theory. I also solve algorithm problems to review data structures and check whether I really understand the concepts.
